title: Evaluating the effect of type 2 diabetes mellitus on CYP450 enzymes and P-gp activities, before and after glycemic control: A protocol for a case–control pharmacokinetic study
author: Neyshaburinezhad, Rouini, et al.
materials: The plasma levels of proinflammatory cytokines including IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α will be quantified by electrochemiluminescence immunoassays using the V-PLEX Proinflammatory Panel 1 Human Kit, QuickPlex SQ120 Imager, and WORKBENCH software (MSD, Rockville, MD). The genetic polymorphism of CYP450 enzymes including CYP2B6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19 and CYP2D6 will be evaluated. Genomic DNA will be extracted from whole blood samples throughout the study in both groups. DNA samples will be used for genetic analyses associated with mentioned CYP450s by using semi-quantitative RT-PCR or other appropriate methods [14,15].

steps.title: Prepare low‑dose cocktail capsules
steps.instruction: Under GLP conditions in the pharmacy laboratory, formulate capsules each containing 25 mg bupropion, 25 mg flurbiprofen, 5 mg omeprazole, 10 mg dextromethorphan, 1 mg midazolam, and 25 mg fexofenadine.

steps.title: Recruit participants and schedule fasting
steps.instruction: Invite poorly controlled diabetic patients and healthy volunteers to the clinical research unit; schedule the experimental day after an overnight fast.

steps.title: Collect baseline clinical samples
steps.instruction: Before dosing, draw two blood samples: one into a serum separator SST II tube for glucose and HbA1c, and one into a K2‑EDTA vacutainer for inflammatory marker assays; send to the laboratory.

steps.title: Administer cocktail with coffee
steps.instruction: Give each participant one prepared capsule together with a cup of coffee containing 100 mg caffeine, and maintain fasting until the final sampling point.

steps.title: Obtain pharmacokinetic blood draws
steps.instruction: Via a venous catheter, collect 4 × blood samples at time 0 (immediately before capsule), and at 1 h, 2 h, and 3 h post‑dose for probe drug and metabolite measurement.

steps.title: Process and store plasma samples
steps.instruction: Immediately centrifuge each blood tube at 4 °C, aliquot the plasma, and store aliquots at –80 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Discharge participants
steps.instruction: After the 3‑hour final blood draw, release participants from the unit.

steps.title: Conduct 3‑month diabetic follow‑up
steps.instruction: For diabetic patients only, implement a 3‑month glycemic‑control program supervised by their physician; record weight and blood glucose monthly; at month 3 repeat the cocktail administration and all covariate measurements. Healthy volunteers receive no further investigation.

steps.title: Extract plasma metabolites
steps.instruction: Perform protein precipitation on thawed plasma aliquots using acetonitrile prior to chromatographic analysis.

steps.title: Quantify probes by HPLC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Measure cocktail probes and their CYP‑specific metabolites in the extracted plasma using the validated high‑performance liquid chromatography/tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC‑MS/MS) method.

steps.title: Run clinical chemistry assays
steps.instruction: Analyze creatinine, AST, ALT, fasting blood sugar (FBS), and HbA1c at the Department of Medical Biochemistry, IMAM KHOMEINI hospital complexes.

steps.title: Measure cytokine concentrations
steps.instruction: Determine plasma IL‑1β, IL‑6, and TNF‑α levels using electrochemiluminescence immunoassays with the V‑PLEX Proinflammatory Panel 1 Human Kit, QuickPlex SQ120 Imager, and WORKBENCH software (MSD, Rockville, MD).

steps.title: Genotype CYP450 polymorphisms
steps.instruction: Extract genomic DNA from whole‑blood samples; assess CYP2B6, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, and CYP2D6 polymorphisms by semi‑quantitative RT‑PCR or other appropriate methods.

steps.title: Perform pharmacokinetic data analysis
steps.instruction: Estimate PK parameters using non‑compartmental analysis in Excel version 6.2.1; calculate single‑point metabolic ratios (metabolite/parent concentration) at each time point; compare pre‑ and post‑control and patient‑healthy ratios with Wilcoxon signed‑rank test; explore correlations with cytokines and clinical variables via simple and multiple linear regression; conduct all statistics in SPSS version 21, considering p ≤ 0.05 as significant.
